spoken_content.text: This is Dr. Tori, your friendly gastroenterologist, and let's talk about nine interesting facts about your gut that sound completely fake, but aren't.
Number one, your gut has its own brain. The enteric nervous system contains millions of neurons and can function largely independently from your brain.

Number two, wild. Your intestines have taste receptors, the same receptor families that are found on your tongue are actually found throughout your GI tract to help detect nutrients and trigger digestion.
Number three, your microbiome helps keep you alive. Gut bacteria help produce vitamins, metabolize bile acids, influence neurotransmitters, and even affect how certain medications work.
Number four, your gut has built-in pacemaker cells. These cells generate electrical rhythms that coordinate peristalsis and move through your digestive tract.
Number five, your microbiome becomes surprisingly stable early in life. After about age three, your gut microbial composition tends to remain relatively stable over time.
Number six, digestive diseases are incredibly common. Globally, billions of people are affected by GI diseases every year. About a third of all diseases have a GI link.
Number seven, disorders of the gut-brain interaction are among the most common medical conditions worldwide, and nearly half the population meets criteria for some of these.

Number eight, stool samples don't tell the whole story. Bacteria found in stool can differ significantly from the organisms actually attached to the intestinal lining. So this poses a challenge for us to understand the gut microbiome even more.

Number nine, your gut is one of the most complex systems in the human body. It relies on constant communication between nerves, immune cells, hormones, microbes, and smooth muscle all happening simultaneously. The best system, if I have to say so myself.
